description.narrative: The project intends to improve access to WASH services for IDPs and host communities through the humanitarian-development nexus approach and contribute to the prevention of water related diseases.

This allocation supports the UNICEF project “Strengthening the resilience of internally displaced populations in Niger through sustainable and equitable access to WASH services.” The project intends to improve access to WASH services for IDPs and host communities through the humanitarian-development nexus approach and contribute to the prevention of water related diseases. UNICEF is a trusted partner to Denmark and central humanitarian actor when it comes to WASH activities.
As an UN agency mandated to aid and protect children, adolescents, and affected households in emergencies, UNICEF is a trusted partner to Denmark. UNICEF leads the WASH cluster in Niger and is therefore a central humanitarian actor when it comes to WASH activities.
Due to its nature as a response to a humanitarian appeal operational results are general and highly aggregated and the MFA contribution is thus reflected in the overall results reporting by the partner. Please refer to the hyperlink below.
https://www.unicef.org/reports
